Open `GWAS_course.Rproj` and work from the project root. Run the chunks in order in a fresh R session.
All data are simulated. Read each summary, run its chunk and compare your result with the expected result.
The linked step pages explain the ideas and provide troubleshooting.

- [0.5 Install the R packages](#step-0-5)

```{r}
#| label: module0_check
if (!file.exists("config.R") && file.exists("../config.R")) setwd("..")
if (!file.exists("config.R") || !file.exists("R/guided.R")) {
  stop("Open GWAS_course.Rproj and run this notebook from the project root.", call. = FALSE)
}
if (requireNamespace("knitr", quietly = TRUE)) knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath("."))
```

## Step 0.1 · Install R {#step-0-1}

We install R, the program that runs the course commands. We choose the version that matches the computer's system and processor.

[Read step 0.1 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-0/step-0-1).

::: {.callout-note title="What you do"}

No R code runs in this step. Check your system and processor in the computer's settings. Open [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/), choose your system and follow its installation instructions. On macOS, choose arm64 for Apple Silicon or x86_64 for Intel. Open R and check that its window appears.

:::

## Step 0.2 · Install RStudio {#step-0-2}

We install RStudio, a program that makes R easier to use. We find the Console area where we will run commands.

[Read step 0.2 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-0/step-0-2).

::: {.callout-note title="What you do"}

No R code runs in this step. Download RStudio Desktop for your system from the [official Posit page](https://docs.posit.co/ide/user/download.html) and follow its installation instructions. Open RStudio and find the Console area with a `>` prompt.

:::

## Step 0.3 · Download and extract the project {#step-0-3}

We download and extract the complete course project. Keeping its files together lets the commands find the files they need.

[Read step 0.3 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-0/step-0-3).

::: {.callout-note title="What you do"}

No R code runs in this step. Download [GWAS_course-2026.4.zip](https://github.com/mgentiluomo/GWAS_training_session/releases/download/project-2026.4/GWAS_course-2026.4.zip). Extract it under C:/ on Windows or your home folder on macOS or Linux, using your system's extraction tool. Open the supplied GWAS_course folder and check that it contains config.R, GWAS_course.Rproj, R, lessons, notebooks and scripts.

:::

## Step 0.4 · Open the project and check R {#step-0-4}

We open the course project and check that R can find its files. We display the system and R version, then try a small calculation to check that commands run.

[Read step 0.4 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-0/step-0-4).

```{r}
#| label: s0-4_project
getwd()  # <1>
stopifnot(file.exists("config.R"), file.exists("R/course.R"))  # <2>
Sys.info()[c("sysname", "release", "machine")]  # <3>
R.version.string  # <4>
2 + 3  # <5>
```

1. Show the folder where R looks for files.
2. Check that the required project files exist.
3. Show the computer's system and processor information.
4. Show the installed R version.
5. Add two numbers to check that R runs commands.

### What each option does

No PLINK options are used in this step.

::: {.callout-tip title="Expected result" collapse="true"}

R prints the path of your project folder. The file checks finish without an error. Your folder path will differ from the author's path.

R prints your system information, its version and the result `[1] 5` from the small calculation. The R version may differ from the validation environment.

`[1] 5`

:::

::: {.callout-note title="PLINK terminal equivalent"}

No PLINK equivalent

:::

2. Copy the PLINK 2 build for your computer into the bin folder and check it.

### What each option does

University of Pisa users request the password through the [data access form](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/data-access) with an email address at unipi.it or one of its subdomains. Other users write to [manuel.gentiluomo@unipi.it](mailto:manuel.gentiluomo@unipi.it). We then download and check the course data, entering the password only in the prompt that hides the letters, never in a file.

[Read step 0.7 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-0/step-0-7).

```{r}
#| label: s0-7_data
#| eval: false
download_course_data()  # <1>
```

1. Download the course data and check that the files are complete and unchanged.

### What each option does

No PLINK options are used in this step.

::: {.callout-tip title="Expected result" collapse="true"}

On the first successful run, R prints `Course data are ready: 108 files verified.` On a later run with verified data, it prints `Course data are already ready: 108 files verified. Nothing to do.` It does not download or ask for the password again. The data are in the folder `data/course/`. The archive and its small manifest file (a list of the files inside) must both match their configured SHA-256 values. R also checks every extracted data file.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="PLINK terminal equivalent"}

No PLINK equivalent

:::

## Step 0.8 · Run the setup check {#step-0-8}

We run the setup check to test the R packages, data files and PLINK 2. PLINK reads 20 DNA positions and writes a report, including a test in a folder whose name contains spaces and non-English letters.

[Read step 0.8 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-0/step-0-8).

```{r}
#| label: s0-8_preflight
settings <- new.env(parent = baseenv())  # <1>
sys.source("config.R", settings)  # <2>
settings$course_settings$tested_plink_version  # <3>
source("scripts/preflight.R")  # <4>
```

1. Create a separate place in R to hold the course settings.
2. Read the course settings from config.R.
3. Show the PLINK version used to test the course.
4. Run the setup checks, including the small PLINK test.

### What each option does

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--bfile` | Reads the BED, BIM and FAM input files named sim2026_lab in data/course/lab_export/. |
| `--autosome` | Keeps only DNA positions on chromosomes 1 to 22. |
| `--thin-count` | Selects 20 DNA positions at random for this small test. |
| `--seed` | Uses 20261111 as the starting number for the random selection so it can be repeated. |
| `--freq` | Writes a report showing how common each version of a DNA letter is at the selected positions. |
| `--out` | Starts the report file names with results/guided/s0-8_probe in the standard project layout; the helper also tests a folder name with spaces and non-English letters. |

Every command also uses `--threads 2` (PLINK runs at most two tasks at the same time) and `--memory 2048` (PLINK uses at most about 2 GB of memory).

::: {.callout-tip title="Expected result" collapse="true"}

The setup check prints one short line per check, with `PASS` or the problem. It keeps the full PLINK output in `results/guided/preflight.txt` (or the folder selected by `COURSE_OUTPUT_DIR`). The tested PLINK version is printed before the checks.

`Preflight passed.`

The guided starting data have 2,016 sample wells and 299,523 variants, representing 2,000 simulated people. PLINK finishes the frequency test on 20 variants. The report can show sex as "ambiguous". This is normal at this stage: the starting FAM has no recorded sex. The probe reads autosomal variants and does not perform the sex check from step 3.3. A path such as `PATHCH~1` in the report is the safe form of a folder with non-English letters.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="PLINK terminal equivalent"}

These commands are shown for reference. Run the R chunk above to follow the course.
R creates any lists needed between PLINK commands. On Windows, use `bin\plink2.exe`.

```sh
bin/plink2 --bfile data/course/lab_export/sim2026_lab --autosome --thin-count 20 --seed 20261111 --freq --out results/guided/s0-8_probe --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

:::

## Step 1.1 · SNPs and genotypes {#step-1-1}

We read a table describing the DNA sites measured by the array. We count its rows and look at site names, chromosome positions and possible DNA letters to understand what the array measures.

[Read step 1.1 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-1/step-1-1).

```{r}
#| label: s1-1
ann <- guided_table(file.path(cfg$data_dir, "array", "sim2026_array_annotation.tsv"))  # <1>
cat(nrow(ann), "rows in the annotation\n")  # <2>
head(ann[c("Name", "Chr", "Position_GRCh38", "Ref_Plus", "Alt_Plus")])
```

1. Read the table describing the DNA sites on the array.
2. Count the rows and show the first site descriptions.

### What each option does

No PLINK options are used in this step.

::: {.callout-tip title="Expected result" collapse="true"}

A table with the site name, the chromosome, the [GRCh38](#glossary-grch38) position and the two alleles on the [plus strand](#glossary-plus-strand). GRCh38 is the version of the human reference genome that gives the positions. The annotation contains 299,523 rows. Array site names are not always rs identifiers.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="PLINK terminal equivalent"}

No PLINK equivalent

:::

## Step 1.2 · How an array measures DNA {#step-1-2}

We find the three laboratory report files and read the first 12 lines of the first report. This shows how the laboratory organises information before we read the recorded DNA results.

[Read step 1.2 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-1/step-1-2).

```{r}
#| label: s1-2
reports <- list.files(file.path(cfg$data_dir, "final_report"), full.names = TRUE)  # <1>
stopifnot(length(reports) == 3L)
readLines(reports[1], n = 12L)  # <2>
```

1. Find the laboratory reports and check that there are three files.
2. Show the first 12 lines of the first report.

### What each option does

No PLINK options are used in this step.

::: {.callout-tip title="Expected result" collapse="true"}

The top of a simulated Final Report: first the header, then the start of the data section. The supplied reports contain genotype calls and GC scores. They do not contain raw intensity data, so you cannot redraw cluster plots in this exercise.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="PLINK terminal equivalent"}

No PLINK equivalent

:::

## Step 1.3 · The Global Screening Array {#step-1-3}

We count the array entries on each chromosome. We also check that the table has 299,523 rows and no repeated site names, so we can recognise the expected starting data.

2. Check the total number of rows and look for repeated site names.

### What each option does

No PLINK options are used in this step.

Autosomes 1 to 22, plus X, Y and MT (mitochondrial DNA). There are 299,523 array entries at the start. The same genomic site can appear under two different names. We review this at step 4.5.

## Step 1.4 · From sample to scanned chip {#step-1-4}

We read the sample sheet and count measurements on each laboratory plate. We count labelled repeat measurements and check that the sheet has 2,016 rows, because one person can have more than one measurement.

[Read step 1.4 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-1/step-1-4).

```{r}
#| label: s1-4
sheet <- read.csv(file.path(cfg$data_dir, "lab_export", "sample_sheet.csv"), colClasses = "character")  # <1>
table(sheet$Plate)  # <2>
sum(nzchar(sheet$Replicate_of))
stopifnot(nrow(sheet) == 2016L)  # <3>
```

1. Read the sample sheet as text to preserve sample labels.
2. Count measurements on each plate and labelled repeat measurements.
3. Check that the sheet contains 2,016 measurements.

### What each option does

No PLINK options are used in this step.

::: {.callout-tip title="Expected result" collapse="true"}

Twenty-one plates, each with 96 wells, give 2,016 measurements. Sixteen wells are labelled as technical replicates. The simulation started from 2,000 people.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="PLINK terminal equivalent"}

No PLINK equivalent

:::

## Step 1.5 · Calling genotypes {#step-1-5}

We read the data section of a laboratory report and display its first rows. We summarise the GC scores, which describe the quality of recorded DNA results, to see what information the report provides.

[Read step 1.5 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-1/step-1-5).

```{r}
#| label: s1-5
lines <- readLines(reports[1], warn = FALSE)  # <1>
start <- match("[Data]", lines)
example <- read.table(text = lines[(start + 1L):length(lines)], sep = ";", header = TRUE, quote = "", check.names = FALSE, colClasses = "character")  # <2>
head(example)  # <3>
summary(as.numeric(example[["GC Score"]]))
```

1. Read the report and find where its data section begins.
2. Read the data as a table with semicolons separating its columns.
3. Show the first rows and summarise the quality scores as numbers.

### What each option does

No PLINK options are used in this step.

::: {.callout-tip title="Expected result" collapse="true"}

The columns are SNP Name, Sample ID, GC Score, Allele1 - Plus and Allele2 - Plus. The examples are short excerpts of reports. They are not the full table of 299,523 sites for every person.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="PLINK terminal equivalent"}

No PLINK equivalent

## Step 1.10 · The formats you will meet most often {#step-1-10}

We read small invented examples to learn what common genetic file fields mean. We examine example conversion commands without running them, so we can understand what conversions preserve and what they may lose.

## Step 2.2 · Convert to PLINK 2 native format {#step-2-2}

We convert the laboratory files to the format that PLINK 2 uses for this course. We check that the conversion keeps every sample and variant, a place in the DNA where people can differ.

[Read step 2.2 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-2/step-2-2).

```{r}
#| label: s2-2
out <- guided_path(cfg, "2.2")  # <1>
run_plink(cfg, c("--bfile", cfg$input, "--make-pgen", "--out", out), paste0(out, c(".pgen", ".pvar", ".psam")))  # <2>
stopifnot(all(guided_counts(out) == c(2016, 299523)))  # <3>
# Course bookkeeping: records the counts for the next step. Do not change.
guided_source_checkpoint(cfg)
```

1. Choose the name for the converted files.
2. Convert the laboratory files to the native PLINK 2 format.
3. Check that all 2,016 samples and 299,523 variants remain.

### What each option does

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--bfile` | Reads the BED, BIM and FAM laboratory files named sim2026_lab in data/course/lab_export. |
| `--make-pgen` | Writes the data as PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files, the native PLINK 2 format. |
| `--out` | Starts the output file names with results/guided/s2-2_state. |

Every command also uses `--threads 2` (PLINK runs at most two tasks at the same time) and `--memory 2048` (PLINK uses at most about 2 GB of memory).

::: {.callout-tip title="Expected result" collapse="true"}

The 2,016 samples and 299,523 variants are all kept. PLINK can mark the [reference allele](#glossary-reference-allele) (REF) as provisional. This happens because a BED file does not say which allele matches the genome reference.

:::

## Step 2.4 · First overview {#step-2-4}

We measure the share of missing DNA results for each sample and each site. These reports help us find possible problems before we choose what to remove.

```{r}
summary(as.numeric(vmiss$F_MISS))
```

## Step 2.5 · Alleles and strand {#step-2-5}

We compare the DNA letters at each site with the supplied reference table. We correct 400 sites read from the opposite DNA strand and remove 3,013 sites whose letters cannot establish a clear match.

[Read step 2.5 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-2/step-2-5).

```{r}
#| label: s2-5
bim <- read_ws(paste0(cfg$input, ".bim"), header = FALSE)  # <1>
ann <- guided_table(file.path(cfg$data_dir, "array", "sim2026_array_annotation.tsv"))
k <- match(bim[[2]], ann$Name)  # <2>
stopifnot(!anyNA(k))
pair <- function(a, b) ifelse(a < b, paste0(a, b), paste0(b, a))  # <3>
observed <- pair(bim[[5]], bim[[6]])
reference <- pair(ann$Ref_Plus[k], ann$Alt_Plus[k])
complement <- chartr("ACGT", "TGCA", reference)  # <4>
complement <- pair(substr(complement, 1, 1), substr(complement, 2, 2))
palindromic <- reference %in% c("AT", "CG")  # <5>
flip <- !palindromic & observed != reference & observed == complement
exclude <- palindromic | (observed != reference & observed != complement)
flip_file <- guided_list(bim[[2]][flip], guided_path(cfg, "2.5", "flip.txt"))  # <6>
exclude_file <- guided_list(bim[[2]][exclude], guided_path(cfg, "2.5", "exclude.txt"))
stopifnot(sum(flip) == 400L, sum(exclude) == 3013L)
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "2.2"), "--flip", flip_file, "--exclude", exclude_file,  # <7>
  "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "2.5")))
stopifnot(all(guided_counts(guided_path(cfg, "2.5")) == c(2016, 296510)))  # <8>
# Course bookkeeping: records the counts for the next step. Do not change.
ops <- data.frame(option = c("--flip", "--exclude"), value = c(flip_file, exclude_file))
guided_register(cfg, "2.5", "2.2", 2016, 296510, operations = ops)
```

1. Read the laboratory variant table and the reference DNA letters.
2. Match every laboratory site to the reference table by its identifier.
3. Put each pair of DNA letters in a consistent order for comparison.
4. Find the reference letter pairs as they would appear on the opposite strand.
5. Identify sites to correct and sites with ambiguous or incompatible letters.
6. Save both lists and check their expected sizes.
7. Correct the listed sites and remove the excluded sites in a new copy.
8. Check that 2,016 samples and 296,510 variants remain.

### What each option does

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files named results/guided/s2-2_state. |
| `--flip` | Uses s2-5_flip.txt to replace each DNA letter by its partner on the opposite strand at 400 sites: A pairs with T, and C with G. |
| `--exclude` | Removes the 3,013 sites listed in s2-5_exclude.txt because their DNA letter pairs are ambiguous or incompatible with the reference table. |
| `--make-pgen` | Saves the corrected data as PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files. |
| `--out` | Starts the corrected file names with results/guided/s2-5_state. |

Every command also uses `--threads 2` (PLINK runs at most two tasks at the same time) and `--memory 2048` (PLINK uses at most about 2 GB of memory).

::: {.callout-tip title="Expected result" collapse="true"}

400 sites are flipped and 3,013 sites are excluded. 2,016 samples and 296,510 variants remain. The planted problem categories overlap, so do not simply add their nominal counts.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="PLINK terminal equivalent"}

These commands are shown for reference. Run the R chunk above to follow the course.
R creates any lists needed between PLINK commands. On Windows, use `bin\plink2.exe`.

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s2-2_state --flip results/guided/s2-5_flip.txt --exclude results/guided/s2-5_exclude.txt --make-pgen --out results/guided/s2-5_state --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

:::

## Step 2.6 · Genome builds and lift-over {#step-2-6}

We convert the DNA positions in a separate exercise from the GRCh37 genome reference to GRCh38. We keep sites that map to the same chromosome, correct opposite-strand letters and check the new positions without changing the main dataset.

[Read step 2.6 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-2/step-2-6).

```{r}
#| label: s2-6
legacy <- file.path(cfg$data_dir, "grch37_exercise", "legacy_grch37")  # <1>
bim37 <- read_ws(paste0(legacy, ".bim"), header = FALSE)
chain <- file.path(cfg$data_dir, "grch37_exercise", "hg19ToHg38.over.chain.gz")  # <2>
require_files(chain)
lifted <- guided_liftover(paste0("chr", bim37[[1]]), bim37[[4]], chain)  # <3>
keep <- !is.na(lifted$position) & lifted$chromosome == paste0("chr", bim37[[1]])
map <- data.frame(ID = bim37[[2]][keep], POS = lifted$position[keep])  # <4>
map_file <- guided_path(cfg, "2.6", "update_map.tsv")
write.table(map, map_file, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE)
keep_file <- guided_list(map$ID, guided_path(cfg, "2.6", "mapped.txt"))
args <- c("--bfile", legacy, "--extract", keep_file, "--update-map", map_file)  # <5>
reverse <- bim37[[2]][keep & lifted$strand == "-"]
if (length(reverse)) args <- c(args, "--flip", guided_list(reverse, guided_path(cfg, "2.6", "reverse.txt")))
run_plink(cfg, c(args, "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "2.6", "grch38")))  # <6>
ann <- guided_table(file.path(cfg$data_dir, "array", "sim2026_array_annotation.tsv"))  # <7>
k <- match(map$ID, ann$Name)
stopifnot(all(map$POS[!is.na(k)] == as.numeric(ann$Position_GRCh38[k[!is.na(k)]])))
print(c(input_sites = nrow(bim37), mapped_same_chromosome = sum(keep), reverse_strand = length(reverse)))  # <8>
```

1. Read the variant positions in the separate GRCh37 exercise.
2. Find the supplied file that links GRCh37 positions to GRCh38 positions.
3. Convert the positions and keep sites that stay on the same chromosome.
4. Save the new positions and the list of sites to keep.
5. Prepare the PLINK options and add a correction for opposite-strand sites if needed.
6. Save the converted exercise separately from the main dataset.
7. Check the new positions against matching sites in the supplied reference table.
8. Show how many sites were read, kept and mapped to the opposite strand.

### What each option does

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--bfile` | Reads the BED, BIM and FAM files named data/course/grch37_exercise/legacy_grch37, containing 10,000 exercise sites. |
| `--extract` | Keeps the 9,970 sites listed in s2-6_mapped.txt that map to the same chromosome in GRCh38. |
| `--update-map` | Reads site identifiers and their new GRCh38 positions from the two columns of s2-6_update_map.tsv. |
| `--flip` | R adds this option when sites map to the opposite DNA strand, using s2-6_reverse.txt to correct the DNA letters at eight sites in this exercise. |
| `--make-pgen` | Saves the converted exercise as PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files. |
| `--out` | Starts the converted exercise file names with results/guided/s2-6_grch38. |

Every command also uses `--threads 2` (PLINK runs at most two tasks at the same time) and `--memory 2048` (PLINK uses at most about 2 GB of memory).

::: {.callout-tip title="Expected result" collapse="true"}

The exercise has 10,000 sites. 9,970 of them map to the same chromosome, and eight of these map to the reverse strand in this chain file. PLINK prints a warning that the base-pair positions are now unsorted. This warning is expected: the new GRCh38 positions are not in the old order. The resulting exercise variants are not sorted by position. Sort them explicitly before any operation that needs sorted input. Mapped positions whose identifier also appears in the course annotation agree with GRCh38. The main 296,510-site state from 2.5 is unchanged. A lift-over can lose sites, so record the mapping counts that are reported.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="PLINK terminal equivalent"}

These commands are shown for reference. Run the R chunk above to follow the course.
R creates any lists needed between PLINK commands. On Windows, use `bin\plink2.exe`.

```sh
bin/plink2 --bfile data/course/grch37_exercise/legacy_grch37 --extract results/guided/s2-6_mapped.txt --update-map results/guided/s2-6_update_map.tsv --flip results/guided/s2-6_reverse.txt --make-pgen --out results/guided/s2-6_grch38 --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

:::

## Step 2.7 · Add phenotype and covariates {#step-2-7}

We match disease status, age and recorded sex to each laboratory well by its identifiers. We save the information table and add disease status and sex to the DNA files so later checks use the right person's information.

[Read step 2.7 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-2/step-2-7).

```{r}
#| label: s2-7
metadata <- guided_metadata(cfg)  # <1>
pheno <- metadata[c("FID", "IID", "SEX", "Age", "Disease")]  # <2>
names(pheno)[1] <- "#FID"
pheno_file <- guided_path(cfg, "2.7", "phenotypes.tsv")
guided_write(pheno, pheno_file)  # <3>
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "2.5"), "--update-sex", pheno_file,  # <4>
  "--pheno", pheno_file, "--pheno-name", "Disease", "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "2.7")))
stopifnot(all(guided_counts(guided_path(cfg, "2.7")) == c(2016, 296510)))  # <5>
# Course bookkeeping: records the counts for the next step. Do not change.
ops <- data.frame(option = c("--update-sex", "--pheno", "--pheno-name"), value = c(pheno_file, pheno_file, "Disease"))
guided_register(cfg, "2.7", "2.5", 2016, 296510, operations = ops)
```

1. Match the sample sheet to each person's disease status, age and recorded sex.
2. Select and name the columns for the sample information file.
3. Save the sample information table.
4. Add recorded sex and disease status to a new copy of the DNA files.
5. Check that all 2,016 samples and 296,510 variants remain.

### What each option does

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the corrected PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files named results/guided/s2-5_state. |
| `--update-sex` | Loads recorded sex from s2-7_phenotypes.tsv by matching the sample identifiers. |
| `--pheno` | Reads the table s2-7_phenotypes.tsv containing the sample identifiers and disease status. |
| `--pheno-name` | Selects the Disease column as the outcome: 1 means a control without the disease and 2 means a case with the disease. |
| `--make-pgen` | Saves PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files with recorded sex and disease status in the sample table. |
| `--out` | Starts the joined file names with results/guided/s2-7_state. |

Every command also uses `--threads 2` (PLINK runs at most two tasks at the same time) and `--memory 2048` (PLINK uses at most about 2 GB of memory).

::: {.callout-tip title="Expected result" collapse="true"}

All 2,016 wells are matched, and 296,510 variants remain. There are 2,000 people before we remove low-quality wells, relatives and ancestry outliers.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="PLINK terminal equivalent"}

These commands are shown for reference. Run the R chunk above to follow the course.
R creates any lists needed between PLINK commands. On Windows, use `bin\plink2.exe`.


## Step 3.1 · Rough cleaning {#step-3-1}

We remove samples and variants with very many missing calls. This first clean prevents the worst failures from distorting the checks that follow.

[Read step 3.1 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-3/step-3-1).

```{r}
#| label: s3-1
input <- guided_path(cfg, "2.8")  # <1>
rough <- guided_path(cfg, "3.1", "samples")
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", input, "--mind", "0.10", "--make-pgen", "--out", rough))  # <2>
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", rough, "--geno", "0.10", "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "3.1")))  # <3>
# Course bookkeeping: records the counts for the next step. Do not change.
ops <- guided_replay_lists(cfg, "3.1", "2.8")
guided_register(cfg, "3.1", "2.8", 2013, 296360, operations = ops)
```

1. Choose the input files and the names for the saved files.
2. Remove samples with more than 10% of calls missing.
3. Remove variants with more than 10% of calls missing.

### What each option does

**Command 1: remove poor samples**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--mind` | Removes samples with more than 10% missing calls. |
| `--make-pgen` | Saves a new dataset as PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

**Command 2: remove poor variants**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--geno` | Removes variants with more than 10% missing calls in the input dataset. |
| `--make-pgen` | Saves a new dataset as PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

Every command also uses `--threads 2` (PLINK runs at most two tasks at the same time) and `--memory 2048` (PLINK uses at most about 2 GB of memory).

::: {.callout-tip title="Expected result" collapse="true"}

Three wells and 150 variants are removed. 2,013 samples and 296,360 variants remain.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="PLINK terminal equivalent"}

These commands are shown for reference. Run the R chunk above to follow the course.
R creates any lists needed between PLINK commands. On Windows, use `bin\plink2.exe`.

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s2-8_state --mind 0.10 --make-pgen --out results/guided/s3-1_samples --threads 2 --memory 2048
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-1_samples --geno 0.10 --make-pgen --out results/guided/s3-1_state --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try other thresholds (optional)" collapse="true"}

This box is not part of the main path. No later step uses it. It does not change your results.

The step makes a rough first clean. `--mind` is the largest share of missing calls that a sample may have. `--geno` is the same limit for a variant. A low value is strict and removes more. A high value is generous. At 0.10 only wells and sites that are clearly broken are removed. The finer checks come later, at steps 3.2 and 4.1, so this first clean can be generous. Each trial below starts from the same input as the step and changes one threshold only.

```{r}
#| label: s3-1_thresholds
#| eval: false
# Optional. Each trial starts from the same input and changes one threshold only. Your results folder is not changed.
thresholds <- c(0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20)
samples <- threshold_counts(cfg, guided_path(cfg, "2.8"), "--mind", thresholds)  # <1>
samples$course_value <- samples$threshold == 0.10
samples
variants <- threshold_counts(cfg, guided_path(cfg, "3.1", "samples"), "--geno", thresholds)  # <2>
variants$course_value <- variants$threshold == 0.10
variants
par(mfrow = c(1, 2)); plot_threshold_trials(samples, "Samples removed"); plot_threshold_trials(variants, "Variants removed")  # <3>
# Optional: add engine = "ggplot2" to plot_threshold_trials() to draw the plot with ggplot2 (install.packages("ggplot2") once first).
```

1. Samples: --mind on the cohort saved at 2.8.
2. Variants: --geno on the samples that remain after --mind 0.10.
3. Plot the removed numbers. The course value is the large diamond.


Plain PLINK 2 command for one trial. It writes only small files with the name that you give to `--out`, never a new dataset:

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s2-8_state --mind 0.05 --make-just-psam --out results/trials/s3-1_trial --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

The log file `results/trials/s3-1_trial.log` states how many samples were removed. To repeat the trial, change the number after `--mind` and use a new `--out` name. For variants, use `--geno` and `--make-just-pvar`, and start from `results/guided/s3-1_samples`. PLINK 2 treats a dosage without a hard call as missing by default (the `dosage` modifier changes this). The course data have hard calls only, so this makes no difference here.

The expected result of the trials:

Samples removed by `--mind`:

| Threshold | Samples removed | Samples remaining |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.01 | 121 | 1,895 |
| 0.02 | 45 | 1,971 |
| 0.05 | 3 | 2,013 |
| **0.1 (course value)** | 3 | 2,013 |
| 0.2 | 3 | 2,013 |

Variants removed by `--geno`, after `--mind 0.10`:

| Threshold | Variants removed | Variants remaining |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.01 | 3,705 | 292,805 |
| 0.02 | 958 | 295,552 |
| 0.05 | 735 | 295,775 |
| **0.1 (course value)** | 150 | 296,360 |
| 0.2 | 130 | 296,380 |

How to read it. Between 0.05 and 0.20 the same three wells are removed. Those wells are so poor that no limit in this range keeps them. Below 0.05 the limit starts to remove good wells too (45 at 0.02 and 121 at 0.01). For variants, a stricter limit removes many more sites. The course value of 0.10 keeps the rough clean generous on purpose.

Expected plot. For `--geno`, the horizontal axis shows the threshold and the vertical axis shows the number of variants removed. A red diamond marks the course value (0.1), where 150 variants are removed. For `--mind`, the horizontal axis shows the threshold and the vertical axis shows the number of samples removed. A red diamond marks the course value (0.1), where 3 samples are removed. The line joins the points in the order of the thresholds, so you can see how fast the count changes. The same plot with ggplot2 looks the same and has a light grid.

:::

## Step 3.2 · Sample call rate {#step-3-2}

We remove samples with more than 2% of their genotype calls missing. This keeps samples with enough information for the later analysis.

[Read step 3.2 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-3/step-3-2).

```{r}
#| label: s3-2
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.1"), "--mind", "0.02", "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "3.2")))  # <1>
# Course bookkeeping: records the counts for the next step. Do not change.
ops <- guided_replay_lists(cfg, "3.2", "3.1")
guided_register(cfg, "3.2", "3.1", 1971, 296360, operations = ops)
```

1. Remove samples with more than 2% of calls missing.

### What each option does

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--mind` | Removes samples with more than 2% missing calls, keeping a call rate of at least 98%. |
| `--make-pgen` | Saves a new dataset as PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

Every command also uses `--threads 2` (PLINK runs at most two tasks at the same time) and `--memory 2048` (PLINK uses at most about 2 GB of memory).

::: {.callout-tip title="Expected result" collapse="true"}

42 more wells are removed. 1,971 samples and 296,360 variants remain.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="PLINK terminal equivalent"}

These commands are shown for reference. Run the R chunk above to follow the course.
R creates any lists needed between PLINK commands. On Windows, use `bin\plink2.exe`.

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-1_state --mind 0.02 --make-pgen --out results/guided/s3-2_state --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try other thresholds (optional)" collapse="true"}

This box is not part of the main path. No later step uses it. It does not change your results.

The call rate of a sample is the share of its calls that are not missing. `--mind 0.02` removes samples with more than 2% missing calls, which is a call rate below 98%. A lower limit keeps more samples but lets in samples with poor DNA. A higher limit removes more samples and may throw away good data. A call rate of 95% to 98% is a common choice in genome-wide studies, and 98% is the stricter end of it. Each trial starts from the cohort saved at 3.1 and changes the limit only.

```{r}
#| label: s3-2_thresholds
#| eval: false
# Optional. Each trial starts from the same input and changes one threshold only.
thresholds <- c(0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20)
trial <- threshold_counts(cfg, guided_path(cfg, "3.1"), "--mind", thresholds)
trial$course_value <- trial$threshold == 0.02
trial
# Plot the removed samples. The course value is the large diamond.
plot_threshold_trials(trial, "Samples removed")
# Optional: add engine = "ggplot2" to plot_threshold_trials() to draw the plot with ggplot2 (install.packages("ggplot2") once first).
```


Plain PLINK 2 command for one trial. It writes only small files with the name that you give to `--out`, never a new dataset:

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-1_state --mind 0.05 --make-just-psam --out results/trials/s3-2_trial --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

The log file `results/trials/s3-2_trial.log` states how many samples were removed. To repeat the trial, change the number after `--mind` and use a new `--out` name.

The expected result of the trials:

| Threshold | Samples removed | Samples remaining |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.01 | 118 | 1,895 |
| **0.02 (course value)** | 42 | 1,971 |
| 0.05 | 0 | 2,013 |
| 0.1 | 0 | 2,013 |
| 0.2 | 0 | 2,013 |

How to read it. At 0.02 the course removes 42 wells. At 0.05 none are removed, so all 42 wells have between 2% and 5% missing calls. At 0.01 another 76 wells go (118 in total). The step is a clear case of a choice: the course value removes the wells that are poor but not broken.

Expected plot. For `--mind`, the horizontal axis shows the threshold and the vertical axis shows the number of samples removed. A red diamond marks the course value (0.02), where 42 samples are removed. The line joins the points in the order of the thresholds, so you can see how fast the count changes. The same plot with ggplot2 looks the same and has a light grid.

:::

## Step 3.3 · Recorded and genetic sex {#step-3-3}

We compare recorded sex with patterns in the X and Y chromosome calls. We remove flagged wells from this teaching analysis because a mismatch needs review before the sample is used.

[Read step 3.3 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-3/step-3-3).

```{r}
#| label: s3-3
split <- guided_path(cfg, "3.3", "par")  # <1>
report <- guided_path(cfg, "3.3", "sexcheck")
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.2"), "--split-par", "b38", "--make-pgen", "--out", split))  # <2>
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", split, "--check-sex", "max-female-xf=0.2", "min-male-xf=0.8",  # <3>
  "max-female-ycount=100", "min-male-ycount=1000", "--out", report))
sexcheck <- guided_table(paste0(report, ".sexcheck"))  # <4>
bad <- sexcheck$IID[sexcheck$STATUS != "OK"]
remove_file <- guided_list(bad, guided_path(cfg, "3.3", "remove.txt"), TRUE)
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", split, "--remove", remove_file, "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "3.3")))  # <5>
# Course bookkeeping: records the counts for the next step. Do not change.
ops <- guided_replay_lists(cfg, "3.3", "3.2", extra = data.frame(option = "--split-par", value = "b38"))
guided_register(cfg, "3.3", "3.2", 1963, 296360, operations = ops)
```

1. Choose names for the chromosome files and sex report.
2. Label the regions shared by the X and Y chromosomes.
3. Compare recorded sex with the X and Y chromosome results.
4. Read the report and list samples that need to be removed.
5. Save the dataset without the flagged samples.

### What each option does

**Command 1: label the shared X and Y regions**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--split-par` | Uses GRCh38 boundaries (b38) to label the shared regions of X and Y separately. |
| `--make-pgen` | Saves a new dataset as PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

**Command 2: compare recorded sex with DNA**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--check-sex` | Compares recorded sex with X chromosome patterns and the number of observed Y calls. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&rarr; `max-female-xf` | Sets 0.2 as the largest accepted X chromosome F value for a recorded female. F measures how homozygous the X chromosome looks, meaning how often the two copies carry the same DNA letter. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&rarr; `min-male-xf` | Sets 0.8 as the smallest accepted X chromosome F value for a recorded male. F measures how homozygous the X chromosome looks. Values near 1 are expected when there is only one X chromosome, as in males. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&rarr; `max-female-ycount` | Accepts at most 100 observed Y calls for a recorded female. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&rarr; `min-male-ycount` | Requires at least 1000 observed Y calls for a recorded male. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

**Command 3: remove samples flagged by the sex check**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--remove` | Removes the samples named in the supplied sample list. |
| `--make-pgen` | Saves a new dataset as PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

Every command also uses `--threads 2` (PLINK runs at most two tasks at the same time) and `--memory 2048` (PLINK uses at most about 2 GB of memory).

::: {.callout-tip title="Expected result" collapse="true"}

Eight flagged wells are removed. 1,963 samples remain. 520 sites are labelled PAR1 or PAR2. The number of variants does not change.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="PLINK terminal equivalent"}

These commands are shown for reference. Run the R chunk above to follow the course.
R creates any lists needed between PLINK commands. On Windows, use `bin\plink2.exe`.

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-2_state --split-par b38 --make-pgen --out results/guided/s3-3_par --threads 2 --memory 2048
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-3_par --check-sex max-female-xf=0.2 min-male-xf=0.8 max-female-ycount=100 min-male-ycount=1000 --out results/guided/s3-3_sexcheck --threads 2 --memory 2048
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-3_par --remove results/guided/s3-3_remove.txt --make-pgen --out results/guided/s3-3_state --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try other thresholds (optional)" collapse="true"}

This box is not part of the main path. No later step uses it. It does not change your results.

The sex check compares the recorded sex with the X chromosome. The X inbreeding coefficient F is close to 0 in females, who have two X chromosomes, and close to 1 in males, who have one. `max-female-xf` is the highest F that a recorded female may have. `min-male-xf` is the lowest F that a recorded male may have. A sample outside its limit is flagged and removed. The course values are 0.2 and 0.8. The Y chromosome limits do not change here. Each trial changes one limit and starts from the cohort saved at 3.2.

```{r}
#| label: s3-3_thresholds
#| eval: false
# Optional. Each trial starts from the same input and changes one limit only. Your results folder is not changed.
females <- sexcheck_counts(cfg, guided_path(cfg, "3.3", "par"), "max-female-xf", c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4))  # <1>
females$course_value <- females$threshold == 0.2
males <- sexcheck_counts(cfg, guided_path(cfg, "3.3", "par"), "min-male-xf", c(0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9))  # <2>
males$course_value <- males$threshold == 0.8
females
males
par(mfrow = c(1, 2)); plot_threshold_trials(females, "Samples flagged", log_x = FALSE); plot_threshold_trials(males, "Samples flagged", log_x = FALSE)  # <3>
# Optional: add engine = "ggplot2" to plot_threshold_trials() to draw the plot with ggplot2 (install.packages("ggplot2") once first).
```

1. Change the female limit, with the other limits at their course values.
2. Change the male limit.
3. Plot the flagged samples. The course value is the large diamond.


Plain PLINK 2 command for one trial. It writes only small files with the name that you give to `--out`, never a new dataset:

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-3_par --check-sex max-female-xf=0.3 min-male-xf=0.8 max-female-ycount=100 min-male-ycount=1000 --out results/trials/s3-3_trial --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

The file `results/trials/s3-3_trial.sexcheck` lists every sample. Count the rows whose `STATUS` is not `OK`. To repeat the trial, change one number and use a new `--out` name. PLINK 2 also checks the Y chromosome counts that you give. They stay the same here.

The expected result of the trials:

Samples flagged when the female limit changes:

| Setting | Samples removed | Samples remaining |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.1 | 14 | 1,957 |
| **0.2 (course value)** | 8 | 1,963 |
| 0.3 | 8 | 1,963 |
| 0.4 | 8 | 1,963 |

Samples flagged when the male limit changes:

| Setting | Samples removed | Samples remaining |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.6 | 8 | 1,963 |
| 0.7 | 8 | 1,963 |
| **0.8 (course value)** | 8 | 1,963 |
| 0.9 | 8 | 1,963 |

How to read it. At the course values, 8 samples are flagged. The male limit makes no difference from 0.6 to 0.9, so the recorded males are clearly separate from the limit. The female limit matters only at the strict end: at 0.1, 6 more samples are flagged (14 in total), which means that 6 recorded females have an X inbreeding coefficient between 0.1 and 0.2. From 0.2 to 0.4 the count does not change. The course value of 0.2 flags the clear cases and leaves the borderline ones for review.

Expected plot. For `max-female-xf`, the horizontal axis shows the setting and the vertical axis shows the number of samples removed. A red diamond marks the course value (0.2), where 8 samples are removed. For `min-male-xf`, the horizontal axis shows the setting and the vertical axis shows the number of samples removed. A red diamond marks the course value (0.8), where 8 samples are removed. The line joins the points in the order of the settings. The same plot with ggplot2 looks the same and has a light grid.

:::

## Step 3.4 · LD pruning {#step-3-4}

We select common DNA sites that are less strongly correlated with each other. This stops groups of similar sites from weighing too much in the sample checks. The full dataset is kept for the association scan.

[Read step 3.4 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-3/step-3-4).

```{r}
#| label: s3-4
regions <- guided_high_ld(cfg)  # <1>
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.3"), "--chr", "1-22", "--maf", "0.05", "--geno", "0.02",  # <2>
  "--exclude", "bed0", regions, "--indep-pairwise", "200kb", "0.2", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "3.4", "prune")))
pruned <- readLines(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "3.4", "prune"), ".prune.in"))  # <3>
stopifnot(length(pruned) == 68800L)
cat(length(pruned), "variants kept by LD pruning\n")
# Course bookkeeping: records the counts for the next step. Do not change.
guided_artifact_checkpoint(cfg, "3.4", c(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "3.4", "prune"), c(".prune.in", ".prune.out")), regions), parent = "3.3")
```

1. Write the list of regions where nearby variants are strongly correlated.
2. Select variants with less similar patterns of DNA letters.
3. Check and print how many variants were selected.

### What each option does

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--chr` | Uses only chromosomes 1 to 22, the autosomes. |
| `--maf` | Keeps variants whose less common allele has a frequency of at least 5%. |
| `--geno` | Keeps variants with no more than 2% missing calls. |
| `--exclude` | Leaves out variants within the listed DNA regions. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&rarr; `bed0` | Reads DNA regions in the BED way: the start of each region is counted from 0 and its end is not included. |
| `--indep-pairwise` | Compares genotype patterns at pairs of sites within windows of 200 kb (200,000 DNA bases). It drops one site of every pair with a squared correlation (r²) above 0.2. A larger r² means that the genotypes of the two sites vary together more closely. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

Every command also uses `--threads 2` (PLINK runs at most two tasks at the same time) and `--memory 2048` (PLINK uses at most about 2 GB of memory).

::: {.callout-tip title="Expected result" collapse="true"}

The `.prune.in` file lists 68,800 sites. The complete analysis state still has 296,360 variants.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="PLINK terminal equivalent"}

These commands are shown for reference. Run the R chunk above to follow the course.
R creates any lists needed between PLINK commands. On Windows, use `bin\plink2.exe`.

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-3_state --chr 1-22 --maf 0.05 --geno 0.02 --exclude bed0 results/guided/s3-4_high_ld.bed0 --indep-pairwise 200kb 0.2 --out results/guided/s3-4_prune --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try other thresholds (optional)" collapse="true"}

This box is not part of the main path. No later step uses it. It does not change your results.

LD pruning keeps a subset of variants that are not strongly correlated. It looks at pairs of variants inside a window. When the squared correlation (r^2) of a pair is above the limit, it drops one variant of the pair. A lower r^2 limit drops more variants. A wider window finds more pairs and drops more variants. The course uses r^2 0.2 and a window of 200 kb. This box only counts the variants that stay. Here "removed" means pruned out. Each trial starts from the same 125,061 variants (autosomal, frequency at least 5%, call rate at least 98%, outside the long-range LD regions) and changes one setting.

```{r}
#| label: s3-4_thresholds
#| eval: false
# Optional. Each trial starts from the same input and changes one setting only. It writes no file in your results folder.
regions <- guided_high_ld(cfg)
r2_limits <- c(0.1, 0.2, 0.5)  # <1>
by_r2 <- sapply(r2_limits, function(r) prune_counts(cfg, guided_path(cfg, "3.3"), regions, r2 = r, window_kb = 200))
windows <- c(50, 200, 1000)  # <2>
by_window <- sapply(windows, function(w) prune_counts(cfg, guided_path(cfg, "3.3"), regions, r2 = 0.2, window_kb = w))
data.frame(r2 = r2_limits, kept = by_r2["kept", ], pruned = by_r2["pruned", ])
data.frame(window_kb = windows, kept = by_window["kept", ], pruned = by_window["pruned", ])
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))  # <3>
plot_threshold_trials(data.frame(threshold = r2_limits, removed = by_r2["pruned", ], course_value = r2_limits == 0.2), "Variants pruned out", log_x = FALSE)
plot_threshold_trials(data.frame(threshold = windows, removed = by_window["pruned", ], course_value = windows == 200), "Variants pruned out")
# Optional: add engine = "ggplot2" to plot_threshold_trials() to draw the plot with ggplot2 (install.packages("ggplot2") once first).
```

1. Change the r2 limit, with a window of 200 kb.
2. Change the window, with an r2 limit of 0.2.
3. Plot the pruned variants. The course value is the large diamond.


Plain PLINK 2 command for one trial. It writes only small files with the name that you give to `--out`, never a new dataset:

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-3_state --chr 1-22 --maf 0.05 --geno 0.02 --exclude bed0 results/guided/s3-4_high_ld.bed0 --indep-pairwise 200kb 0.5 --out results/trials/s3-4_trial --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

The number of lines of `results/trials/s3-4_trial.prune.in` is the number of variants kept. To repeat the trial, change `200kb` or `0.5` and use a new `--out` name.

The expected result of the trials:

Variants pruned out and kept when the r^2 limit changes (window 200 kb):

| Setting | Variants removed | Variants remaining |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.1 | 76,459 | 48,602 |
| **0.2 (course value)** | 56,261 | 68,800 |
| 0.5 | 24,308 | 100,753 |

Variants pruned out and kept when the window changes (r^2 limit 0.2):

| Setting | Variants removed | Variants remaining |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 50 | 46,961 | 78,100 |
| **200 (course value)** | 56,261 | 68,800 |
| 1000 | 57,375 | 67,686 |

How to read it. The r^2 limit has a large effect. At 0.1 the pruning keeps 48,602 variants, at 0.2 it keeps 68,800 and at 0.5 it keeps 100,753. The window has a smaller effect: 50 kb keeps 78,100, 200 kb keeps 68,800 and 1,000 kb keeps 67,686. More variants are not better for the checks that use this list. A larger set contains more correlated variants, which count several times. A smaller set carries less information. The course value is a middle choice that leaves enough sites for the heterozygosity check, the relatedness check and the PCA.

Expected plot. For `r2 limit`, the horizontal axis shows the setting and the vertical axis shows the number of variants removed. A red diamond marks the course value (0.2), where 56,261 variants are removed. For `window (kb)`, the horizontal axis shows the setting and the vertical axis shows the number of variants removed. A red diamond marks the course value (200), where 56,261 variants are removed. The line joins the points in the order of the settings. The same plot with ggplot2 looks the same and has a light grid.

:::

## Step 3.5 · Heterozygosity {#step-3-5}

We check whether each sample has unusually many or few sites with two different DNA letters. We remove samples with unusually many such sites and flag those with unusually few for review, because an unusual value alone does not prove an error.

[Read step 3.5 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-3/step-3-5).

```{r}
#| label: s3-5
report <- guided_path(cfg, "3.5", "het")  # <1>
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.3"), "--extract", paste0(guided_path(cfg, "3.4", "prune"), ".prune.in"), "--het", "--out", report))  # <2>
het <- guided_table(paste0(report, ".het"))  # <3>
f <- as.numeric(het$F)
mean_f <- mean(f); sd_f <- sqrt(mean((f - mean_f)^2))
low <- het$IID[f < mean_f - 3 * sd_f]  # <4>
high <- het$IID[f > mean_f + 3 * sd_f]
guided_list(high, guided_path(cfg, "3.5", "flag_high.txt"), TRUE)  # <5>
remove_file <- guided_list(low, guided_path(cfg, "3.5", "remove.txt"), TRUE)
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.3"), "--remove", remove_file, "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "3.5")))  # <6>
print(c(mean_F = mean_f, SD_F = sd_f))  # <7>
print(c(low_removed = length(low), high_flagged = length(high)))
# Course bookkeeping: records the counts for the next step. Do not change.
ops <- guided_replay_lists(cfg, "3.5", "3.3")
guided_register(cfg, "3.5", "3.4", 1950, 296360, operations = ops)
```

1. Choose the name for the report of matching DNA letters.
2. Measure matching DNA letters using the selected variants.
3. Read the report and calculate the average and spread of F.
4. Find samples with unusually low or high F values.
5. Save the high F review list and the low F removal list.
6. Save the dataset without the low F samples.
7. Print the average and spread of F, then the numbers of flagged samples as whole numbers.

### What each option does

**Command 1: measure matching DNA letters**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--extract` | Uses only the variants named in the supplied variant list. |
| `--het` | Reports, for each sample, the observed and expected numbers of genotypes with two matching DNA letters, and calculates F from them. R reads the F values and calculates the review thresholds. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

**Command 2: remove samples with unusually high heterozygosity**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--remove` | Removes the samples named in the supplied sample list. |
| `--make-pgen` | Saves a new dataset as PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

Every command also uses `--threads 2` (PLINK runs at most two tasks at the same time) and `--memory 2048` (PLINK uses at most about 2 GB of memory).

::: {.callout-tip title="Expected result" collapse="true"}

13 wells with low F are removed. Eight wells with high F are flagged and kept. The mean F is approximately 0.0078. The population SD is approximately 0.0298. 1,950 samples remain.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="PLINK terminal equivalent"}

These commands are shown for reference. Run the R chunk above to follow the course.
R creates any lists needed between PLINK commands. On Windows, use `bin\plink2.exe`.

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-3_state --extract results/guided/s3-4_prune.prune.in --het --out results/guided/s3-5_het --threads 2 --memory 2048
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-3_state --remove results/guided/s3-5_remove.txt --make-pgen --out results/guided/s3-5_state --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try other thresholds (optional)" collapse="true"}

This box is not part of the main path. No later step uses it. It does not change your results.

The statistic F compares the homozygosity that we see in a sample with the homozygosity that we expect from the allele frequencies. A very low F means too many heterozygous calls, which can come from contamination. A very high F means too few, which can come from related parents or a different ancestry. The course removes samples with F more than 3 standard deviations (SD) below the mean. It only flags, and keeps, samples with F more than 3 SD above the mean. The trials change the number of SD from 2 to 4. They use the same F values.

```{r}
#| label: s3-5_thresholds
#| eval: false
# Optional. The trials use the table of F values that the step wrote. No PLINK run is needed.
multipliers <- c(2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4)
trial <- het_counts(guided_table(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "3.5", "het"), ".het")), multipliers)
trial$course_value <- trial$threshold == 3
trial
# Plot the removed samples. The course value is the large diamond.
plot_threshold_trials(trial, "Samples removed", log_x = FALSE)
# Optional: add engine = "ggplot2" to plot_threshold_trials() to draw the plot with ggplot2 (install.packages("ggplot2") once first).
```


Plain PLINK 2 command for one trial. It writes only small files with the name that you give to `--out`, never a new dataset:

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-3_state --extract results/guided/s3-4_prune.prune.in --het --out results/trials/s3-5_trial --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

This command writes the F table (`results/trials/s3-5_trial.het`). The limit itself is not a PLINK option: the course calculates it in R from the table. To repeat a trial in R, change the number 3 in the rule for `low` and `high` at the step.

The expected result of the trials:

| SD from the mean | Samples removed | Samples remaining | Samples flagged |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | 13 | 1,950 | 13 |
| 2.5 | 13 | 1,950 | 11 |
| **3 (course value)** | 13 | 1,950 | 8 |
| 3.5 | 13 | 1,950 | 5 |
| 4 | 13 | 1,950 | 0 |

How to read the two numbers. "Removed" counts wells with an F value below the mean by more than the chosen number of SD. They have too many heterozygous calls, so the course takes them out of the data. At the course value of 3 SD, 13 wells are removed. "Flagged" counts wells with an F value above the mean by more than the chosen number of SD. They have too few heterozygous calls. The course keeps them in the data and only lists them for review. At the course value, 8 wells are flagged. Now the table. The same 13 wells are removed at every limit from 2 to 4 SD. This group is clearly separate from the rest. The number of flagged wells changes from 13 to 0, so it depends more on the rule than on the data. Flagged wells are kept, so this choice does not change the cohort.

Expected plot. For `F cutoff (standard deviations)`, the horizontal axis shows the threshold and the vertical axis shows the number of samples removed. A red diamond marks the course value (3), where 13 samples are removed. The line joins the points in the order of the thresholds, so you can see how fast the count changes. The same plot with ggplot2 looks the same and has a light grid.

:::

## Step 3.6 · Relatedness and duplicates {#step-3-6}

We compare pairs of samples to find repeated measurements and close relatives. We apply the stated removal rules, and keep the person with the better call rate, so that repeated or closely related people do not distort the later association analysis.

[Read step 3.6 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-3/step-3-6).

```{r}
#| label: s3-6
report <- guided_path(cfg, "3.6", "king")  # <1>
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.5"), "--extract", paste0(guided_path(cfg, "3.4", "prune"), ".prune.in"),  # <2>
  "--make-king-table", "--king-table-filter", "0.0442", "--out", report))
kin <- guided_table(paste0(report, ".kin0"))  # <3>
kin <- kin[order(-as.numeric(kin$KINSHIP)), ]
metadata <- guided_metadata(cfg)  # <4>
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.5"), "--missing", "sample-only", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "3.6", "missing")))
sample_missing <- guided_table(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "3.6", "missing"), ".smiss"))
lower_call_rate <- function(a, b) {
  fa <- as.numeric(sample_missing$F_MISS[match(a, sample_missing$IID)]); fb <- as.numeric(sample_missing$F_MISS[match(b, sample_missing$IID)])
  if (fa > fb) a else if (fb > fa) b else max(a, b)
}
remove <- character()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(kin))) {  # <5>
  a <- kin$IID1[i]; b <- kin$IID2[i]; value <- as.numeric(kin$KINSHIP[i])
  if (value > 0.354) {  # <6>
    if (endsWith(a, "_R2") || endsWith(b, "_R2")) {  # <7>
      remove <- union(remove, if (endsWith(a, "_R2")) a else b)
    } else {
      ai <- match(a, metadata$IID); bi <- match(b, metadata$IID)  # <8>
      same <- identical(unname(unlist(metadata[ai, c("SEX", "Age", "Disease")])),
                        unname(unlist(metadata[bi, c("SEX", "Age", "Disease")])))
      remove <- union(remove, if (same) lower_call_rate(a, b) else c(a, b))  # <9>
    }
  } else if (value > 0.177 && !a %in% remove && !b %in% remove) remove <- union(remove, lower_call_rate(a, b))  # <10>
}
remove_file <- guided_list(remove, guided_path(cfg, "3.6", "remove.txt"), TRUE)  # <11>
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.5"), "--remove", remove_file, "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "3.6")))  # <12>
# Course bookkeeping: records the counts for the next step. Do not change.
ops <- guided_replay_lists(cfg, "3.6", "3.5")
guided_register(cfg, "3.6", "3.5", 1920, 296360, operations = ops)
```

1. Choose the name for the report comparing pairs of samples.
2. Compare pairs using the selected variants.
3. Read the pairs and put the closest matches first.
4. Read the sample details, measure the missing data of every sample and start an empty removal list.
5. Review each pair to decide which samples to remove.
6. Treat the closest matches as repeated samples.
7. Remove the labelled repeat when its name ends in _R2.
8. Compare sex, age and disease status for unlabelled repeats.
9. Keep one matching record or remove both conflicting records.
10. Keep one person from each remaining closely related pair.
11. Write the removal list.
12. Save the dataset without the listed samples.

### What each option does

**Command 1: compare pairs of samples**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--extract` | Uses only the variants named in the supplied variant list. |
| `--make-king-table` | Estimates how closely related each pair of samples is and writes a table. |
| `--king-table-filter` | Writes only pairs whose kinship score is above 0.0442. The kinship score measures how closely two people are related. This value is an approximate boundary for third-degree relatives such as first cousins. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

**Command 2: measure the missing data of every sample**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--missing` | Measures the share of missing genotype calls and writes a table with one row per sample. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&rarr; `sample-only` | Writes only the sample table, not the variant table. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

**Command 3: remove repeated or closely related samples**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--remove` | Removes the samples named in the supplied sample list. |
| `--make-pgen` | Saves a new dataset as PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

Every command also uses `--threads 2` (PLINK runs at most two tasks at the same time) and `--memory 2048` (PLINK uses at most about 2 GB of memory).

::: {.callout-tip title="Expected result" collapse="true"}

There are 19 duplicate-class pairs and ten first-degree pairs. In total, 30 records are removed. 1,920 samples remain. Pairs can overlap, because one person can be in more than one pair. For this reason, the pair counts are not counts of unique people.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="PLINK terminal equivalent"}

These commands are shown for reference. Run the R chunk above to follow the course.
R creates any lists needed between PLINK commands. On Windows, use `bin\plink2.exe`.

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-5_state --extract results/guided/s3-4_prune.prune.in --make-king-table --king-table-filter 0.0442 --out results/guided/s3-6_king --threads 2 --memory 2048
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-5_state --missing sample-only --out results/guided/s3-6_missing --threads 2 --memory 2048
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-5_state --remove results/guided/s3-6_remove.txt --make-pgen --out results/guided/s3-6_state --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try other thresholds (optional)" collapse="true"}

This box is not part of the main path. No later step uses it. It does not change your results.

The kinship coefficient estimates how much DNA two samples share. The usual KING cutoffs are 0.354 for repeated samples and identical twins, 0.177 for first-degree relatives, 0.0884 for second-degree relatives and 0.0442 for third-degree relatives (Manichaikul et al. 2010, doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btq559). This step does not use `--king-cutoff`. It writes the table of pairs with `--make-king-table` and `--king-table-filter 0.0442`, and a rule in R decides who to remove. The trials change the cutoff for relatives. Pairs above 0.354 are always treated as repeats.

```{r}
#| label: s3-6_thresholds
#| eval: false
# Optional. The trials use the table of pairs that the step wrote. No PLINK run is needed.
cutoffs <- c(0.0442, 0.0884, 0.177, 0.354)
kin <- guided_table(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "3.6", "king"), ".kin0"))
trial <- data.frame(threshold = cutoffs, removed = kinship_counts(kin, guided_metadata(cfg), cutoffs, guided_table(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "3.6", "missing"), ".smiss"))))
trial$course_value <- trial$threshold == 0.177
trial
# Plot the removed samples. The course value is the large diamond.
plot_threshold_trials(trial, "Samples removed")
# Optional: add engine = "ggplot2" to plot_threshold_trials() to draw the plot with ggplot2 (install.packages("ggplot2") once first).
```


Plain PLINK 2 command for one trial. It writes only small files with the name that you give to `--out`, never a new dataset:

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-5_state --extract results/guided/s3-4_prune.prune.in --king-cutoff 0.177 --out results/trials/s3-6_trial --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--king-cutoff` removes one member of each pair above the cutoff with a greedy rule, and it writes two lists of sample IDs (`.king.cutoff.in.id` and `.king.cutoff.out.id`). Its count can differ a little from the course rule, which also treats repeats separately. To repeat the trial, change the number after `--king-cutoff`.

The expected result of the trials:

| Kinship cutoff | Samples removed | Samples remaining |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.0442 | 30 | 1,920 |
| 0.0884 | 30 | 1,920 |
| **0.177 (course value)** | 30 | 1,920 |
| 0.354 | 20 | 1,930 |

How to read it. The cutoffs 0.0442, 0.0884 and 0.177 give the same 30 removed samples. In this simulated cohort no extra pair lies between 0.0442 and 0.177. At 0.354 only repeated samples are removed (20), and the ten first-degree pairs stay in the data. Real cohorts usually have many more distant relatives, so the counts would then differ.

Expected plot. For `KING kinship cutoff`, the horizontal axis shows the threshold and the vertical axis shows the number of samples removed. A red diamond marks the course value (0.177), where 30 samples are removed. The line joins the points in the order of the thresholds, so you can see how fast the count changes. The same plot with ggplot2 looks the same and has a light grid.

:::

## Step 3.7 · Batch effects {#step-3-7}

We compare the fraction of successful genotype calls across laboratory plates. We remove the faulty plate in these simulated data because samples processed together can share technical problems.

[Read step 3.7 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-3/step-3-7).

```{r}
#| label: s3-7
report <- guided_path(cfg, "3.7", "missing")  # <1>
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.6"), "--missing", "sample-only", "--out", report))  # <2>
missing <- guided_table(paste0(report, ".smiss"))  # <3>
metadata <- guided_metadata(cfg)
plate <- metadata$Plate[match(missing$IID, metadata$IID)]
median_missing <- tapply(as.numeric(missing$F_MISS), plate, median)  # <4>
print(sort(1 - median_missing))
worst <- names(which.max(median_missing))  # <5>
stopifnot(worst == "P14")
remove_file <- guided_list(missing$IID[plate == worst], guided_path(cfg, "3.7", "remove.txt"), TRUE)  # <6>
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.6"), "--remove", remove_file, "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "3.7")))  # <7>
# Course bookkeeping: records the counts for the next step. Do not change.
ops <- guided_replay_lists(cfg, "3.7", "3.6")
guided_register(cfg, "3.7", "3.6", 1844, 296360, operations = ops)
```

1. Choose the name for the missing-call report.
2. Count missing calls for each sample.
3. Read the report and match each sample to its laboratory plate.
4. Calculate and print the middle call rate for each plate.
5. Find the plate with the most missing calls and check its name.
6. Write the list of samples from the faulty plate.
7. Save the dataset without samples from that plate.

### What each option does

**Command 1: measure missing calls by sample**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--missing` | Writes a report of missing genotype calls. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&rarr; `sample-only` | Writes one row per sample and skips the report for variants. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

**Command 2: remove samples from the faulty plate**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--remove` | Removes the samples named in the supplied sample list. |
| `--make-pgen` | Saves a new dataset as PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

Every command also uses `--threads 2` (PLINK runs at most two tasks at the same time) and `--memory 2048` (PLINK uses at most about 2 GB of memory).

::: {.callout-tip title="Expected result" collapse="true"}

Plate P14 has a median call rate of approximately 98.56%. The other plates have 99.84%. The 76 remaining wells of plate P14 are removed. 1,844 samples and 296,360 variants remain.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="PLINK terminal equivalent"}

These commands are shown for reference. Run the R chunk above to follow the course.
R creates any lists needed between PLINK commands. On Windows, use `bin\plink2.exe`.

```sh

bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-6_state --remove results/guided/s3-7_remove.txt --make-pgen --out results/guided/s3-7_state --threads 2 --memory 2048
```
